record.context_brief: positive curvature in compatible symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Let (M, ω) be a symplectic manifold, let J be an almost complex structure compatible with ω, and let g(X,Y)=ω(X,JY) be the associated Riemannian metric. If g has positive sectional curvature, must M be diffeomorphic to complex projective space CP^n? More strongly, must M be symplectomorphic to CP^n?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. On a symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\), we can consider an almost complex structure \(J\) which may not be integrable, and the compatible Riemannian metric \(g(X,Y)=\omega(X,JY)\). Suppose this \(g\) has positive sectional curvature, does it imply that \(M\) is diffeomorphisc to \(\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^n\) ? Moreover, how about “symplectomorphic” ?

artifact.category_tag: positive sectional curvature in symplectic geometry
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $J$ be an almost complex structure on $M$ that is compatible with $\omega$ in the sense that $\omega(JX,JY)=\omega(X,Y)$ for all tangent vectors $X,Y$ and $\omega(X,JX)>0$ for every nonzero $X$. (Note that $J$ is not assumed to be integrable.) Define the associated Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ by $g(X,Y)=\omega(X,JY)$. Assume that $g$ has positive sectional curvature, i.e., for every point $p\in M$ and every $2$-plane $\sigma\subset T_pM$, the sectional curvature $K_g(\sigma)>0$.

(a) Must $M$ be diffeomorphic to the complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$?

(b) More strongly, must $(M,\omega)$ be symplectomorphic to $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\omega_{\rm FS})$, where $\omega_{\rm FS}$ denotes the Fubini–Study symplectic form?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the area of positive sectional curvature within compatible symplectic/almost-Kähler geometry. Standard results (e.g., Synge-type theorems, Berger-type rigidity) constrain such manifolds, and the analogous Hopf-type conjecture for Kähler manifolds with positive sectional curvature is itself unresolved in general. No published proof was found that resolves either the diffeomorphism or symplectomorphism version of the question for almost-Kähler metrics, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Almost complex manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Any symplectic manifold has a compatible almost complex structure; conversely a compatible almost complex structure plus a symplectic form yields an almost-Kähler structure.
status_evidence.claim: Background confirming the almost-Kähler setup of the question.

status_evidence.title: Kähler manifold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Hopf conjecture (in one form) asks whether a closed Kähler manifold of positive sectional curvature must be biholomorphic to CP^n; this is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Even the integrable (Kähler) version of the analogous question is open, indicating the almost-Kähler version is also open.
